output.summary: KEP-5004 lets cluster admins advertise DRA devices as extended resources via a DeviceClass field (extendedResourceName), so existing pods requesting extended resources can be dynamically allocated DRA devices. The KEP reached status implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: The problem is that transitioning from device plugins to DRA requires changing every workload spec, and admins want to convert nodes gradually. The design has kube-scheduler pick either device-plugin extended resources or DRA devices, and record DRA allocations in a special per-pod ResourceClaim that the kubelet and DRA drivers consume unchanged. The discussion centers on whether the scheduler or a controller should create that claim; the scheduler-created approach was the one the thread moved toward, with the lifecycle question deferred to before beta.

alternatives.option: Mutating webhook that rewrites extended resource requests into DRA resource claims
alternatives.why_not: Requires cluster admins to deploy and maintain a mutation webhook with rewrite rules; the KEP rejects it for configuration and maintenance overhead.

alternatives.option: Client CLI tool that rewrites extended resource requests in pod YAML into resource claims
alternatives.why_not: Adds extra overhead to the application deployment flow for developers and operators.

alternatives.option: ResourceClaim created in advance by the ResourceClaim controller for pods using extended resources
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (pohly) argued it locks the pod to DRA nodes and forces the controller to predict scheduling, which breaks gradual node-by-node migration; this was a discussed alternative, not the chosen design.

alternatives.option: Singleton ResourceClaim per namespace tracking all pods' extended resource allocations
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (mortent, johnbelamaric) noted drivers need to map allocations to specific container requests, so a per-pod claim was proposed instead.

evidence.quote: This KEP provides a solution to enable cluster administrators to advertise the dynamic resources (in `ResourceSlice`) as extended resource via `DeviceClass`.
Enable cluster administrators to transition to DRA gradually at their own pace, possibly one node a time
Why don't we make the scheduler responsible for creating a per-pod ResourceClaim for the extended resource requests in a pod if and only if needed?
If the "ResourceClaim for extended resources" gets created in advance, the pod is locked to being scheduled to nodes which use DRA.
Deferring the discussion before beta whether scheduler should create resource claim sounds good to me.
